top_stories.title: Bitcoin Crashes Amid Tech Stock Selloff
points: Bitcoin fell roughly 5-5.8% in 24 hours, dropping from above $80,000 to under $76,000 (around $75,954), as a selloff in semiconductor, AI, and tech stocks spread into crypto markets.
Hundreds of millions of dollars in leveraged long positions (borrowed bets wagering on price increases) were liquidated during the crash.
Wednesday's earlier bounce above $80,000 was driven largely by short sellers covering positions (closing bets that a price would fall) rather than new buying interest, making the rally short-lived.
The decline reflects crypto's continued correlation with tech-heavy equity markets, particularly Nasdaq-listed companies like Nvidia and Tesla.

unique_angles.point: Tesla fell about 9% from a $385 close to around $349 after Democrats' midterm sweep raised concerns about slowing AI data center construction; prediction markets show 82% odds Tesla drops to $330 or below by November 30, and 39% odds it falls below $300.
Microsoft rose Wednesday even as Nvidia and Tesla fell, before a broad Wall Street selloff hit Thursday as markets digested election implications.

Washington's new Democratic Congressional majority is preparing a broader crypto market structure bill (a law setting regulatory rules for crypto markets), though its timing and contents remain uncertain.

items.title: Moscow Exchange to List Bitcoin
points: Moscow Exchange will launch Bitcoin trading starting December 1, 2026.
The move marks a significant institutional adoption milestone in Russia and could boost institutional investor participation in crypto.

headlines: Bitcoin crashed from $80k to under $76k (down 5.8%) as post-election rally unwinds, with hundreds of millions in leveraged long positions liquidated.
Tech stocks plummeted Thursday after initial split Wednesday, as Democrats' midterm sweep sparked AI concerns and Tesla fell 9% to $349.
Democrats' new Congressional majority is preparing a broader crypto market structure bill, raising questions about long-awaited industry regulations.
Prediction markets show 82% odds Tesla drops to $330 or below by end of November, citing Democratic policy concerns over AI data center expansion.
Bitcoin's rally proved short-lived as much of Wednesday's bounce came from short sellers covering positions rather than fresh buying interest.

sections.title: Bitcoin's Volatile Post-Election Swing
points: 1. Bitcoin bounced above $80,000 on Wednesday after Democrats swept Congress, but most gains came from short sellers rushing to cover bets (closing short positions rather than new buyers entering).
2. Thursday's crash to $76,000 (a 5.8% drop in 24 hours) wiped out hundreds of millions in leveraged long bets, which are large borrowed positions betting on price increases.
3. Current price of $75,954 reflects broader market volatility tied to post-election uncertainty and tech sector concerns.
4. The whiplash demonstrates how quickly crypto can reverse when leverage unwinds, even after seemingly positive political developments.

sections.title: Tech Stock Rout Compounds Election Uncertainty
points: 1. Microsoft surged Wednesday while Nvidia and Tesla declined, followed by a broad Wall Street selloff Thursday as markets digested election implications.
2. Tesla fell approximately 9% from Wednesday's $385 close to around $349 Thursday, with some winning Democrats pledging to slow AI data center construction.
3. Prediction market odds show 82% probability Tesla drops to $330 or below by November 30, with 39% odds of falling below $300.
4. AI policy concerns from the new Democratic majority appear to be driving tech sector volatility more than crypto-specific factors.

sections.title: Democrats Push Crypto Market Structure Bill
points: 1. Washington's new Democratic majority is preparing to advance a broader crypto market structure bill covering regulatory frameworks.
2. The timing and contents remain uncertain, raising questions about what form long-awaited industry rules will eventually take.
3. This regulatory push comes as crypto markets demonstrate high volatility and leverage concentration, potentially influencing any new rules' strictness.
4. Market participants face uncertainty about whether regulation will tighten or provide needed clarity for institutions.
